title: Philadelphia Flyers set to sign goalie Dan Vladar to five-year extension on July 1
content:
The Philadelphia Flyers are set to sign goaltender Dan Vladar to a five-year contract extension with an average annual value of $5.5 million, league sources (granted anonymity to speak about talks that aren’t public) have told The Athletic’s Pierre LeBrun.

The contract cannot be announced until July 1, per league rules.

Vladar, who will turn 29 on Aug. 20, is set to enter the second of a two-year, $6.7 million ($3.35 million AAV) contract he signed with the Flyers on July 1, 2025. His new contract will take him through the 2031-32 season.

In his first season with the Flyers, Vladar won the Bobby Clarke Award as the team’s most valuable player, going 29-14-7 with a 2.42 goals-against average and .906 save percentage in 52 games. In 10 playoff games, Vladar was 4-6 with a 2.18 GAA and .922 save percentage with two shutouts, including a remarkable 42-save performance in the Flyers’ 1-0 series-clinching Game 6 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins in the first round.

Vladar, who joined the Flyers as free agent because he saw an opportunity to become a No. 1 for the first time in his NHL career, made it known in his final media conference of the season that he was hopeful a contract extension was in his future.

“Yeah, and if you ask the same question to (Flyers general manager Daniel Briere), I’m going to be watching to see what he says,” Vladar said with a grin.

“He didn’t slow down and he was just as good or even better in the playoffs,” Briere said after the season. “That was really exciting to see. It makes us believe he could be the answer here for hopefully a few more years.”

In six NHL seasons, Vladar is 78-48-23 with a 2.80 goals-against average and .898 save percentage with the Flyers, Calgary Flames and Boston Bruins. He was originally selected by the Bruins in the third round with the 75th pick of the 2015 draft.

Vladar will be paired in net next season with Joseph Woll, who was acquired by the Flyers from the Toronto Maple Leafs as part of a trade on June 17.
